questions.question: Why can't you pass a plain function as a prop from a Server Component to a Client Component?
options: Functions are too large to send over the network
Props crossing the server-client boundary must serialize like JSON, and functions/class instances can't serialize (Server Actions are a special case)
It's a security restriction with no technical reason
You actually can, this is a myth
questions.explanation: There's no way to send executable code from server to client as plain data. Server Actions work because Next.js wires them up as special callable references, not as ordinary functions.

questions.question: Why pass a Server Component as `children` into a Client Component instead of making the whole tree a Client Component?
options: It has no real benefit, it's just a style preference
It keeps the server-rendered content (and its server-only dependencies) out of the client JS bundle while still nesting it inside interactive UI
Client Components cannot accept children at all
questions.explanation: The interactive shell stays a small Client Component; the expensive/server-only content is rendered on the server and passed down as already-resolved JSX, never becoming part of the client bundle.

questions.question: What happens if you try to use `useState` inside a Server Component?
options: It works exactly like in a Client Component
It fails — hooks require a client-side lifecycle that a Server Component, which is just an async function returning JSX, doesn't have
It works, but only in production builds
It silently becomes a Client Component automatically
questions.explanation: Hooks like useState, useEffect, and useContext only work in Client Components; a Server Component has no client-side lifecycle to hook into.

questions.question: What's the risk of importing a server-only module (like a database client) into a file marked "use client"?
options: There is no risk, imports are always safe
It can fail to bundle, or worse, leak server secrets into client-shipped JavaScript
It only affects build time, never runtime
It automatically gets stripped out safely by Next.js
questions.explanation: Server-only code and secrets are not meant to reach the browser; importing them into client code risks exposing credentials or logic that should stay server-side.
